THE ANOMALY WAS MOSTLY DARK-TONED IN APPEARANCE AND INCLUDED A SMALL SILVER SHIMMERY SECTION AT THE SOUTHEASTERNMOST END, THAT INDICATED POSSIBLE THICKER OIL. Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: NISSAN NORTH AMERICA
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 35.962481, -86.495233 (Approximated from street_address)
Report Description
ON TUESDAY 2/14/2012 DURING PRODUCTION, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT A PURGE SOLVENT COLLECTION HEADER LOCATED INSIDE THE PAINT SYSTEM 3 PAINT PLANT WAS CLOGGED. THIS RESULTED IN EIGHT PURGE POTS OVERFLOWING INTO THE FLOOD SHEET IN PAINT BOOTH 1, WHICH IS A WATER RECIRCULATION SYSTEM USED FOR PAINT SOLIDS COLLECTION. WE HAVE CALCULATED THAT 19 GALLONS (139 POUNDS) OF WASTE PURGE SOLVENT WAS RELEASED INTO THE FLOOD SHEET WHICH RESULTED IN THE SOLVENT BEING EMITTED INTO THE AIR. THE WASTE PURGE SOLVENT IS A BLEND OF MANY SOLVENTS WHICH CARRIES THE HAZARDOUS WASTE CODES OF D001, F003, AND D035. THE MOST STRINGENT RQ THRESHOLD OF THESE WASTE CODES IS 100 POUNDS FOR THE F003 WASTE THEREFORE THIS SPILL EXCEEDED THE THRESHOLD FOR REPORTING.

THE DIESEL FUEL IMPACTED AN AREA OF ASPHALT/CONCRETE PARKING LOT AND LOADING DOCK. IN THE LOADING DOCK AREA THERE IS A STORM DRAIN IMPACTED BY THE RELEASE. THE RELEASE IS CONTAINED TO THE STORM DRAIN. THE STORM DRAIN LEADS TO AN ON SITE RETENTION POND WHICH SHOWS NO EVIDENCE OF A SHEEN AT THIS TIME. THE RESPONSIBLE PARTY CONTACTED ERTS TO OVERSEE ENVIRONMENTAL OPERATIONS. ERTS DISPATCHED ENVIRONMENTAL RESTORATION TO THE SITE TO PERFORM REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES. ENVIRONMENTAL RESTORATION IS CURRENTLY ON SITE PERFORMING REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES.

properties.title: NRC Report: Diesel Fuel 1 near Sitka, AK
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 895344 - Medium Affected: SUBSURFACE - Suspected Responsible Party: US COAST GUARD
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 895344
Incident Time: 2009-01-09 18:00:00
Nearest City: Sitka, AK
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: DIESEL FUEL 1
Medium Affected: SUBSURFACE
Suspected Responsible Party: US COAST GUARD
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 16 gallons
AVIATION AIRPORT RAMP OIL WATER SEPARATOR AND IT'S OUTFALL WERE COVERED BY SNOW PILED AND BLOWN TO THAT AREA DURING SNOW REMOVAL OPERATIONS. OIL WATER IS ROUTINELY INSPECTED AND SOUNDED AND WATER CUT WEEKLY BY CG ENVIRONMENTAL STAFF. ON 1/9/09 OWS HAD TO BE DUG OUT. IT WAS WARMING AND RAINING. OWS OUTFALL WAS DISCOVERED TO BE FROZEN, WITH SOME OIL DISCHARGED THROUGH THE TOP OF THE OWS MANHOLE. THE DRAIN WAS THAWED AND THE OWS WAS RETURNED TO NORMAL. A SOUNDING AND WATER CUT TAKEN AFTER THE OWS WAS ABLE TO STABILIZE SHOWED A LOSS OF APPROXIMATELY 15.5 GALLONS TO DOWNSTREAM A POND/LAGOON. SORBENTS WERE PLACED IN THE CONCRETE SUMP, DRAINAGE DITCH, AND LAGOON AS SOON AS THE OUTFALL WAS DISCOVERED TO BE FROZEN AND APPROXIMATELY 14 GALLONS OF OIL HAS BEEN RECOVERED. SORBENTS ARE BEING LEFT IN THE AREA TO RECOVER RESIDUAL OIL IF POSSIBLE.
